computer.intro: After installing tmex on another server or computer, there are two ways to connect: join an existing relay (Hub), or make this machine the relay so other machines can join it.

install.title: Install tmex
install.description: Run the install script on the target machine (installs Bun automatically; Linux needs tmux ≥ 3.0). The terminal prints the access address when done.

mode.title: Choose how to connect
mode.host: Use this machine as the relay

hub.title: Prepare the relay server
hub.description: Relay (Hub) needs a public HTTPS address; if none, set one up via "Use this machine as the relay".

token.title: Generate a join token
token.description: In the relay's tmex open Settings → Multi-node Mesh → Node management, click Add → Generate join token, then copy the join command. The token is valid for 10 minutes.
token.label: Join token (valid for {{minutes}} minutes)
token.meshDescription: Generate a join token here, then copy the command in the next step. The token is valid for 10 minutes.

run.title: Join from the new machine
run.description: Run the join command in the new machine's terminal (example below; use the command you copied):
run.ready: Run this command in the new machine's terminal:

confirm.title: Confirm the join
confirm.description: Back on the relay's Node management page, click Confirm join. The new machine appears in the device list after it restarts.
confirm.meshDescription: Once the new machine runs the command, confirm the join here. It appears in the device list after it restarts.
confirm.done: The new machine has joined; it appears in the device list after it restarts.

hub.title: Make it the relay
hub.description: Open Settings → Multi-node Mesh, choose "Make this machine the Hub", enter the address from the previous step as the Hub public URL, create the first account and restart.
hub.warning: The Hub public URL cannot be changed afterwards. Decide on the final domain first.

status.self: This machine is already the Hub. Public address: {{url}}

guide.title: Install the CA on your devices
guide.intro: Download tmex-ca.crt, then follow the steps for your platform. Check the fingerprint above after installing.

macos.title: macOS
macos.steps: Double-click tmex-ca.crt to open Keychain Access, put it in the System keychain, then open the entry and set "When using this certificate" to "Always Trust".

ios.title: iOS / iPadOS
ios.steps: AirDrop or mail the file to the device and install the profile, then enable it under Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings.

windows.title: Windows
windows.steps: Run certmgr.msc, go to Trusted Root Certification Authorities → Certificates → All Tasks → Import and pick tmex-ca.crt. Firefox keeps its own store, so import it there as well.

android.title: Android
android.steps: Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate. The browser trusts user CAs; other apps only do so if they opt in.

linux.title: Linux
linux.steps: Copy the file to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/tmex-ca.crt and run sudo update-ca-certificates (Debian/Ubuntu), or to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ and run sudo update-ca-trust (Fedora/RHEL).
